Now `parseCircleAt` splits at the verb and reads the subject ONCE (`readCircleSubject`: `one` named/contextual, `pair` conjoined/plural-named/unnamed, Hebrew and English) and every target list — including the line-first order's object — through the one `tangentTargets` (an unnamed «למעגל» is a contextual circle piece). A named subject introduces its circle(s), as the singular always did; a pair with a target list makes each circle tangent to it.

**(2) The branch-word list was hard-coded three times**, each with a fixed position: «משיק מבחוץ למעגל K», «חיצונית/פנימית», «מבחוץ זה לזה» all failed. Now one table (`TANGENT_BRANCH`) and one peeler (`peelMods`) — a branch word, «זה לזה» or «בנקודה T» comes off either end of the sentence or straight after the verb, in any order. A modifier with no circle-to-circle relation to land on («משיק לציר ה-x מבחוץ»), a reciprocal on a singular subject, or two contradictory branch words decline the sentence — never a dropped word.

**(3) The touch point** («בנקודה T») is determined, so it is a derived point: `touch-point {a, b}`, the first `DerivedRule` with TWO curve parents (`curveParentsOf` replaces the single-curve read at the existence check and the reference walk). Closed form `K ± r_K·û`, choosing the candidate at distance r_M from M, so it follows whichever touch the configuration drew — including an unstated one cycling under «הציגו תצורה אחרת». 0 DOF (locked: 5 DOF with or without it); a letter that already exists becomes a condition on it through `derived-at` (#1320). Not more than a derived point, so no escalation.

**(4) P1 — an open bound judged exactly** (`inDomain`, `engine/types.ts`: `v <= d.min`). «…מבחוץ» then «…מבפנים» forces r = 0; the descent converged to r ≈ 8.6e-11, which `r > 0` accepted — drawn green with an invisible circle. Pre-existing on main in the same class: «M(3,0)» + «מעגל M משיק לציר ה-x» (r ≈ 7.4e-10, green). Fix at the judge: `inDomain(d, v, floor)`, and stage two's `admissible` passes `openBoundFloor` = `SOLVE_RESOLUTION` (ADR-AG-136's "indistinguishable by this solver") × the figure's scale (point spread, or the largest parameter magnitude when larger — a radius is part of the extent). Open min, open max and excluded values use the one floor; sampling and display keep `floor = 0`. A converged-to-zero radius is now inadmissible, the best admissible effort leaves the contradicting given unsatisfied, and it is refused on its sentence. Both reported cases now refuse (either order, plural too; the axis case too). The #1423 "letter already defined" hint no longer fires for a circle sentence about a circle that already exists (its centre letter NAMES the circle), so the refusal is the plain «לא נמצאה תצורה…» naming the sentence.

**(5) Operator ruling 2026-09-29 — concentric circles are not tangent.** The internal row |MK| − |r−R| was satisfied at d = 0 with r = R. Tangency presupposes a line of centres, so d > 0 is part of the relation, judged like every open bound at the solver's resolution relative to the radii: inside it the row reports the larger of the miss and the gap (zero-free at d = 0, continuous at the floor). Every spelling, with or without a branch word, is refused naming the statement. A `distinct` selector was tried first and rejected: selectors are reported only at 0 DOF (#1071) and a lowered selector has no blame path, so T19b (radii still free) stayed green.

**Measured.** The sheet's 8 red cases and their neighbours green through `decideSubmit`; 65 locks in `issue-1504-circle-tangency.test.ts` (48 new: 13 subject spellings, 11 branch positions × 12 seeds, 4 declines, 6 touch-point spellings × 12 seeds with T on both circles, DOF, the existing-letter condition, 4 zero-radius refusals + the axis case + the judge, 7 concentric refusals). **24-seed sweep** over every distinct `derive` input the analytic lane makes that carries an open bound or a circle tangency (102 figures, collected by instrumenting the lane): whole-rate **2232/2448 before, 2232/2448 after, no figure changed**; total time 17.2 s → 18.1 s.

**Deliberately not built.** «נתון כי …» (the analytic-wide «נתון כי» opener gap — not tangency's). A touch point on a LINE or axis tangency («מעגל M משיק לציר ה-x בנקודה T») — declined, not dropped; its own capability. «המעגלים משיקים לציר ה-x» without names (which circles?) — declined.

**Consequences.** `parser/parseAnalytic.ts` (`readCircleSubject`, `peelMods`, `TANGENT_BRANCH`, `parseCircleAt` rewritten; the separate subject regexes gone), `engine/derived.ts` (`touch-point`, `curveParentsOf`, `touchPoint`), `engine/sameDerivation.ts`, `engine/apply.ts` (`at`, two-curve existence check), `engine/solve.ts` (concentric floor, `describeRule`, curve refs), `engine/types.ts` (`inDomain` floor, `tangent-circles.at`), `engine/evaluate.ts` (`openBoundFloor`, `spanOf`), `app/submit.ts` (restated-centre hint), `parser/catalogAnalytic.ts` (two rows, not featured). Lock: `issue-1504-circle-tangency.test.ts`.
## ADR-AG-168 — One curve-operand resolver: named, contextual, equation and plural spellings of «on» and «crossing» (#1429)

**Status:** accepted · 2026-09-28 · external prod review relayed by the operator (2026-09-27) · round #1510. Numbered 168 because 167 was minted the same day on `feat/1504-circle-tangency`.

**Requirements:** [02c](02c-requirements-analytic.md) R119 (crossing spellings noted) · **Design:** [04c](04c-design-analytic.md#a-point-on-an-object-and-the-carrier-that-holds-it-adr-ag-029-adr-ag-032)

**Context.** *"«P על המעגל I» fails although «הנקודה P נמצאת על המעגל» works … the canvas even marks the intersections, but you can't name them."* Re-measured at pickup (round worktree @ `21ddb55f`): the issue's whole table stood — point-on-named-circle `not-handled` in six spellings; «ו-l2»/«והישר» never joined a crossing (the connective demanded spaces); the distributive «של הישרים l1 ו-l2», the bare «של הישרים», and both verb forms `not-handled`; an equation operand beside the NAMED circle carrying that equation refused `unknown-reference` leaking `curve-anon…` (#1145's class). Root cause, class first: **"which curve does this operand name" had three hand-written resolvers** — `incidenceOn` (crossings), the `ON_OBJECT` handler, `ON_KIND` — each knowing a different subset.

**Decision.** (1) **`incidenceOn` is THE operand resolver** and the `ON_OBJECT` handler delegates to it; what stays per-sentence is what the rulings genuinely split: a bounded noun in a point-on sentence is a `between` selector (#1069/#1168), a crossing's is the hard extent (#1286). A contextual kind noun answers a `kind` marker that lowers to the same fold-resolved `on-kind` both sentences share; a numeral circle reads digits and Romans onto ONE id («המעגל 1» is «המעגל I»). (2) **The equation-identity arm** (ADR-AG-023/#1342): an equation operand rides the `on-curve` constraint (`eqSrc`/`eq`, spelling-only — stripped at apply, excluded from `canonicalConstraint`), and the apply boundary resolves it against the figure's equation curves at the probe environments (`resolveCurveByEq`), minting `stated: false` only when nothing matches — so «עם המעגל ‎(x-3)²+(y-4)²=9‎» beside circle I is a reference to I, and `curve-anon` ids no longer reach refusals. (3) **The connective** admits the clitic as written (`INTERSECT_JOIN`: «עם», «ו », «ו-», attached «והישר») with a lookahead keeping prose out. (4) **The other spellings normalise to the canonical sentence** (`intersectionSpellings` → `viaCanonical`, the #1495 seam): distributive plural, short form, both verb orders; the bare «של הישרים» lowers to the new M1 fact `crossing-kind` (exactly two of the kind, else `ambiguous-shape` — `on-kind`, one arity up). An ordinal over an unresolved operand refuses. (5) Catalog: the crossing sentence and «P על המעגל I» — NOT featured: the derived section's six seats are full and #1347 keeps them the operator's call (the rows feed the LLM grammar either way). **Not built, by the plan's own marker:** «…בנקודות A ו-B» — the two-letter assignment question is the operator's, filed as **#1512** (`needs-operator`).

**Measured.** The issue's 18-row table green through real `parse → derive`; 23 locks (`issue-1429-curve-operand.test.ts`) including the identity arm both ways, the ambiguous refusals, #1175/#1255 unchanged, and no refusal containing `curve-anon`.

**Consequences.** `parser/parseAnalytic.ts` (`incidenceOn` widened + delegation, `INTERSECT_JOIN`, `intersectionSpellings`, `withLineNoun`, `ROMAN_OF_DIGIT`), `engine/solve.ts` (`on-curve.eqSrc/eq`, canonical key), `engine/apply.ts` (`resolveCurveByEq`, the on-curve resolution step, `crossing-kind`), `engine/types.ts`, `parser/catalogAnalytic.ts`. Lock: `issue-1429-curve-operand.test.ts`.
## ADR-AG-169 — Radius, focus, directrix and perimeter: sayable and askable (#1432)

**Status:** accepted · 2026-09-28 · external prod review relayed by the operator (2026-09-27) · round #1510. Numbered 169 beside the round's parallel branches (167 on `feat/1504`, 168 on `fix/1429`).

**Requirements:** [02c](02c-requirements-analytic.md) R87 family (the ask lane's vocabulary) · **Design:** [04c](04c-design-analytic.md) ask lane + conic roles

**Context.** *"The Ask box is narrow. It can't answer radius, focus, … perimeter."* Re-measured at pickup: every given in the issue's table `not-handled`, every ask unreadable — while `parabolaFocus`/`parabolaDirectrix`/`ellipseFoci` and the circle's r were computed all along and shown only in the panel's folded detail (#1212).

**Decision.** (1) **The radius is a given three ways**: at CREATION («נתון מעגל O שרדיוסו 5», «מעגל שמרכזו O ורדיוסו 5» — the circle is born with a literal r, no param minted, 2 DOF not 3); POST-HOC on a free `circle-at` («רדיוס המעגל (I|O)? הוא 5», M1 fact `radius-of` resolved through the tangent-of name chain) — the free sym is SUBSTITUTED and its parameter retired (a substitution, not a solver row: the radius became a given, and the fold reapplies it deterministically); as a RESTATEMENT on a determined circle — checked at the probe environments, `conflicting-restatement` when false. A computed `circle-thru` refuses `out-of-scope` by name. (2) **«F מוקד הפרבולה»** is a derived point — `DerivedRule` grew `parabola-focus` (closed form inlined in `derived.ts`; curves.ts depends on it, so importing back would cycle), resolved to THE parabola at M1 exactly as «O מרכז המעגל» resolves its circle. (3) **«משוואת המדריך היא x=-2»** is a claim checked against the parabola's own directrix per probe; a parameter-dependent directrix refuses `out-of-scope` (pinning `a` from the directrix is not built — a loud refusal, never a false conflict). (4) **The asks** — «רדיוס המעגל (I)?», «מוקד הפרבולה»/«המוקד», «מדריך הפרבולה», «מוקדי האליפסה», «היקף (המשולש)? ABC» — read the same atoms: radius through `isKnowledge` over the figure's circle; focus/directrix/foci through `knownCurve` (a parameterised conic answers the honest `null`); the PERIMETER delegates to the compound-length ask («היקף ABC» ≡ «AB+BC+CA» by construction).

**Measured.** 19 locks (`issue-1432-measure-roles.test.ts`): every given row of the issue's table (pin → DOF 3→2, claims true/known false/refused, focus at (2,0), directrix both ways, ambiguous with no parabola), every ask row answering its value, perimeter ≡ compound sum, the two honest nulls (parameterised focus, free radius).

**Consequences.** `engine/derived.ts` (+every rule switch: `sameDerivation`, `describeRule`), `engine/types.ts` (`radius-of`, `focus-of`, `directrix-eq`), `engine/apply.ts` (three M1 cases), `parser/parseAnalytic.ts` (creation tail, `parseMeasureRoles`), `app/ask.ts` (four ask atoms + the perimeter delegation), `parser/catalogAnalytic.ts` (two rows, not featured). Lock: `issue-1432-measure-roles.test.ts`.

### ADR-AG-169 Am. 1 — the pre-played sheet: one role reader, one ask normaliser, one substitution seam (2026-09-29 pre-play)

**Status:** accepted · 2026-09-29 · the pre-played sheet on PR #1513 (20 cases, 10 red) and the operator's go-ahead to fix the five open PRs the same day.

**Requirements:** [02c](02c-requirements-analytic.md) R122 (new) · **Design:** [04c](04c-design-analytic.md#measure-roles-one-reader-one-ask-normaliser-one-substitution-seam-adr-ag-169-am-1)

**Context — the classes the sheet found, measured on the merged branch.** (a) **Honesty:** «רדיוס המעגל הוא -3», «שרדיוסו -3», «שרדיוסו 0» were ACCEPTED and the circle vanished with no message: the post-hoc pin substituted the value into `r_O` and retired the parameter without reading its domain `{min: 0, minOpen}`, and the creation tail put the literal in with no parameter at all (`apply.ts` radius-of; `circleAtFacts`). (b) **One spelling per role:** each given and each ask was its own hand-written regex, so «רדיוס המעגל הוא 5» worked while «רדיוס המעגל 5», «שווה 5», «אורך הרדיוס הוא 5», «ברדיוס 5», «שמרכזו (2,3) ורדיוסו 5» did not; «מדריך הפרבולה» answered while «משוואת המדריך» fell to `EQUATION_OF` and reported a missing curve named «המדריך». (c) **Openers:** every ask — the new four AND the old ones («מהו AB», «AB?», «מהי משוואת הישר AB») — was unreadable behind «מהו/מצא את/…?», because only `LOCUS_OF` listed openers, inside its own pattern. (d) **The issue's own table was not covered:** perimeter as a given, the focus by coordinates, «מוקד הפרבולה הוא F». (e) **Wrong remedy:** every contextual refusal taught «שטח הדלתון ABCD הוא 24». (f) **Latent:** the ask printed the directrix as `x = −c/a`, true only for a vertical directrix.

**Decision.**
1. **One substitution seam checks the domain** (`admitStated`, `engine/apply.ts`). Every stated value replacing a domained symbol passes it: a constant outside the domain refuses `out-of-domain` (new code, carrying the domain for the locale to word — «הוא חייב להיות גדול מ-0»); a lone parameter («שרדיוסו a») inherits the domain through the one `param` merge (an empty intersection — «a<0» then «שרדיוסו a» — refuses); any other parametric expression is refused only when no probe environment admits it. The CREATION tail now lowers to the same `radius-of` fact as the post-hoc sentence (applied last, by exact `circleId`), so the two spellings cannot differ, and the substitution now replaces the symbol **everywhere** — objects and constraints — which fixes a second defect the sweep exposed: «נתון מעגל O משיק לציר ה-x» then «רדיוס המעגל הוא 3» drew r = 3 while the tangency kept solving the retired `r_O`.
2. **One role reader** (`readRoleRef`, `parser/parseAnalytic.ts`) reads the noun phrase of each role — radius («(אורך) (ה)רדיוס (של) (ה)מעגל (I)»), focus («(שיעורי) (ה)מוקד (הפרבולה|האליפסה)»), foci, directrix («(משוואת) (ישר) (ה)מדריך (הפרבולה)»), perimeter («היקף (ה<noun>)? (ABC)?», the nouns DERIVED from the shape registry + «מצולע»). The GIVEN is `<role> <copula>? <value>` in either order (`roleSplits`: the one copula set, `=`/`:`, or a first/last value token); the ASK is the role phrase alone. Sayable ⇒ askable by construction.
3. **One ask normaliser** (`normaliseAsk`, `app/ask.ts`) strips the enumerated openers («מצא/חשב את», «מהו/מהי/מהם/מהן», «מה הוא/היא/הם/הן», «מה», find/calculate/compute/what is) and the closer («?», «= ?») before EVERY rule; `LOCUS_OF` no longer lists them. The class, not the new atoms: «מהו AB», «AB?», «מה השיפוע של AB», «מהי משוואת הישר AB» all answer now.
4. **The givens the table asked for:** the perimeter is a REAL constraint — with vertices it lowers straight to the side-sum `length-eq` «AB+BC+CA=12» carries (plus the named polygon, #1080); by noun alone or bare («היקף המשולש הוא 12», «ההיקף הוא 12») to the new M1 fact `perimeter-of`, resolved by `ringsNamed` (`engine/shapes.ts` — the same resolver the perimeter ask uses); DOF 2 → 1, measured. The focus by coordinates («מוקד הפרבולה הוא (2,0)») mints the point (the #1263 tool-named point) and names it the focus: a fixed parabola judges it (a false focus is `unsatisfiable`), a **parameterised parabola is pinned** — «y²=2px» with focus (2,0) closes the DOF and answers directrix x = −2 (the engine's existing `derived-at` lowering; nothing new was needed). «מוקד הפרבולה הוא F», «הנקודה F היא מוקד הפרבולה» read through the same splits. The centre by coordinates («נתון מעגל שמרכזו (2,3) ורדיוסו 5», «…O(2,3)…», «בנקודה (2,3)»): the mint placeholder is now replaced inside composite ids too (`viaCanonical`, `resolveMints`), since the circle carries it in `circle-at-…` and `r_…`.
5. **The remedy follows the host.** `ambiguous-shape` carries `host: {kind, found, need?}` from every CURVE-kind contextual site (radius, focus, directrix, tangency, diameter, on-kind, crossing-kind, perimeter); the locale picks `errHost.{none|many|pair}.{kind}` through one chooser (`app/hostKey.ts`) — name the circle, define the parabola first, write the vertices. The polygon-noun sites (area, meet) carry no host and keep the kite example they were written for. The ask gains the twin outcome `host` («אין בשרטוט פרבולה», «יש בשרטוט יותר ממעגל אחד — כתבו את שם המעגל»), and a NAMED circle the figure lacks answers `missing`.
6. **The directrix is derived, not assumed.** One role-line formatter (`roleLineText`/`directrixText`, `app/curveText.ts`) prints the directrix LINE (`x = …` when vertical, else explicit), used by the ask and the panel row (whose focus now reads its own y too); the given is judged line against line (proportional homogeneous triples), so no branch assumes a vertical directrix when an upward parabola enters scope.

**Deliberately not built** (each named for a successor issue): **«R=5» / «r=5»** — a single capital letter is a legal point name (R is a common third point) and a lower-case letter a parameter symbol, so the sentence collides by construction; left `not-handled` and locked. **«F מוקד האליפסה» / «F1 ו-F2 מוקדי האליפסה»** — understood, refused `out-of-scope`: there is no ellipse-focus derived rule. **Pinning a parameter from the DIRECTRIX** («y²=2px», «משוואת המדריך היא x=-2») stays the loud `out-of-scope` (the focus pins; the directrix-to-parameter lowering is not built). **A parametric non-lone radius** («שרדיוסו 2a») is accepted when some probe admits it — its domain cannot be carried back onto `a`. **A radius claim on a computed circle** (`circle-thru`) stays `out-of-scope`.

**Measured.** Merged branch (origin/main @ `ffbd99e7`), ~110 phrasings re-swept through `decideSubmit` + `ask`. Locks: `issue-1432-measure-roles.test.ts` grows from 19 to 129 — the seven out-of-domain refusals (each its own assertion) and the worded bound, the lone-parameter domain, the constraint-reaching substitution, 26 opener/closer asks including the pre-existing asks and the locus, 14 role-reader asks, 8 post-hoc and 8 creation radius spellings, the R/r refusal, 5 directrix and 5 focus spellings, the focus by coordinates fixed/false/parameterised, the ellipse-focus refusal, 5 perimeter spellings with DOF 2 → 1, the contextual perimeter, the host refusals with their worded remedy (never «דלתון») and the kite case unchanged, the six ask-host twins, and the derived directrix.

**Consequences.** `engine/apply.ts` (`admitStated`, `noHost`/`HostRef`, `out-of-domain`, `substituteSym`, `sameLineTriple`, `perimeter-of`), `engine/types.ts` (`perimeter-of`, `radius-of.circleId`), `engine/shapes.ts` (`ringsNamed`, `ANY_POLYGON_NOUN`), `engine/derive.ts` (host/domain on faults; embedded mint ids), `parser/parseAnalytic.ts` (`readRoleRef`, `roleSplits`, `parseMeasureRoles`, the radius tail + centre slot, `viaCanonical` embedded sentinel), `app/ask.ts` (`normaliseAsk`, `roleAnswer`, `host`), `app/curveText.ts` (`roleLineText`, `directrixText`), `app/hostKey.ts` (new), `app/submit.ts`, `store/useAnalyticStore.ts`, `App.tsx`, `i18n/index.ts` (`errHost.*`, `askHost.*`, `errOutOfDomain`, `range.*`), `parser/catalogAnalytic.ts` (two rows, not featured).

**Merged with #1504 (ADR-AG-167 Am. 1), 2026-09-29.** Two mechanisms touched the same ground and were made ONE, not stacked. (a) The circle CREATION grammar (centre coordinates, the radius tail) is no longer a second pattern beside #1504's circle-subject reader: `readCircleSubject`'s one-circle form now carries `placed`/`coords`/`radius`, so «נתון מעגל O ברדיוס 3 משיק לציר ה-x», «המעגל ברדיוס 5 משיק לציר ה-x» and «מעגל M שרדיוסו 2 משיק למעגל O מבחוץ» are one subject + one verb; `circleAtFacts` emits the circle relations and then `radius-of` LAST so the substitution reaches every constraint carrying `r`; the separate post-hoc «המעגל ברדיוס 5» pattern was deleted (the subject reader reads it); a pair subject carrying a radius or coordinates is declined, not half-read. (b) The radius DOMAIN has one predicate, `inDomain`: #1504's solve judge passes the scale-relative `openBoundFloor`, this seam judges a STATED value with the default floor 0 (exact). The `tangent-circles` contextual refusal carries its host (`errHost.pair.circle` / none / many), joining the host-remedy class.

## ADR-AG-170 — A conic may be named, every reference site inherits it, and a declined completion is not «not understood» (#1271, #1336)

**Status:** accepted · 2026-09-28 · operator request 2026-09-20 (*"נתונה פרבולה I - y^2=2x"*) + ruling (*"we need to support all such forms of writing"*) · round #1510. Numbered 170 beside the round's parallel branches (167–169).

**Requirements:** [02c](02c-requirements-analytic.md) R44 family (naming) · **Design:** [04c](04c-design-analytic.md) curve naming

**Context.** Only a circle could carry a name; a parabola or ellipse got an anonymous content id no sentence could reach, so with two parabolas drawn *"the focus of which one?"* had no writable answer. His own spelling «נתונה פרבולה I - y^2=2x» refused `out-of-scope` — and «פרבולה I: y^2=2x» (#1336) burned a paid escape call to produce the very name-preserving line the tool then declined, shown as «לא הצלחתי להבין» for a sentence the tool understood perfectly.

**Decision.** (1) **One naming clause per language for BOTH conics** (`matchCurve` — a third copy per kind is the #1233/#1267 shape): optional numeral (anonymous keeps the content id), gender tolerated («נתון פרבולה» meant the parabola), and the connective set the textbook prints — «שמשוואתה», «:», «-», «היא» — with the «-» connective added to the NAMED circle and line clauses too (his own punctuation refused `out-of-scope` before). Ids `parabola-I`/`ellipse-I` beside `circle-I`; names «פרבולה I». (2) **Reference sites**: `curveByName` answers the numeral for the new ids (ask lane, «משוואת הפרבולה I»); the crossing operand and «P על הפרבולה I» resolve the named conic to the SAME id (never a second object). (3) **The catalog carries the naming row**, which is also what teaches the LLM lane the spelling — the #1336 class (*"every capability gap must be visible to the model"*) closed for this construct by removing the gap itself. (4) **A `rejected` fallback outcome carries the refusal KEY** and the app says the honest middle — «הבנתי את המשפט, אבל הכלי עדיין לא תומך במהלך הזה» (`errLlmUnderstood`) — never «not understood» for an understood sentence, and never the model's own line (#1251).

**Measured.** 15 locks (`issue-1271-1336-conic-naming.test.ts`): eight naming spellings × kinds × connectives asserting the resulting ID, two parabolas separately referable, anonymous forms unchanged, restatement one object, «P על הפרבולה I» and a crossing through the named conic building at the true roots, «פרבולה I: y^2=2x» parsing directly (the escape never fires), and the rejected-completion code carried.

**Consequences.** `parser/parseAnalytic.ts` (the conic-naming clause, «-» connectives, named-conic operands), `engine/types.ts` (`curveByName`), `app/fallback.ts` (`rejected.code`), `App.tsx` + `store` + `i18n` (`errLlmUnderstood`), `parser/catalogAnalytic.ts`. Lock: `issue-1271-1336-conic-naming.test.ts`.

### ADR-AG-170 Amendment 1 — 2026-09-29 pre-play: one noun table, one numeral, the noun checked, one connective grammar

**Status:** accepted · 2026-09-29 · the pre-played sheet on PR #1514 (20 cases, 9 red) and the operator's go-ahead to fix it.

**Requirements:** [02c](02c-requirements-analytic.md) R7 (now built), R51 (numeral note) · **Design:** [04c](04c-design-analytic.md) — the circle-numeral paragraph (now every numeral-named curve, `engine/names.ts`) and the `Curve.kind` expectation (now checked)

**Context.** The branch was 73 commits behind `main`; #1429 (ADR-AG-168) had landed "one curve-operand resolver" in the meantime. Re-measured after the merge through the real `decideSubmit` path: the three verb crossings («הישר l1 חותך את הפרבולה I בנקודה A», «…והפרבולה I נחתכים…», «A נקודת החיתוך של הישר l1 עם הפרבולה I») were green for parabolas, ellipses and named circles once the named-conic operand sat inside main's resolver. Five defects remained, each an instance of a class:

1. **An internal id reached the student.** «P על הפרבולה I» on an empty canvas answered «הנקודה parabola-I עדיין לא הוגדרה» — wrong noun AND raw id. Root: `refKindOf` (`engine/apply.ts`) knew only the `line-`/`circle-` prefixes and `statedName` stripped only those; the App's key table had no parabola/ellipse row either. Three hand-written copies of "what does this id call itself".
2. **The noun was never checked against the equation.** «פרבולה I שמשוואתה x^2+y^2=16» drew a circle labelled «פרבולה I»; `main` already did the same for «מעגל I שמשוואתו y^2=2x» and every anonymous form. Root: `classify(k, expect)` received the claim and never compared it (its one use of `expect` was an odd `not-a-curve` for an ellipse under the circle noun) — 02c R7 was written and never built.
3. **Two numerals for one name.** «פרבולה 1» and «פרבולה I» minted two objects, and `main` had the mirror bug for circles («מעגל 1» minted `circle-1`, «P על המעגל 1» resolved to `circle-I`). Root: the mint used the token verbatim while #1429's `asRoman` normalised only the circle operand.
4. **Two copies of the naming clause had drifted.** The circle clause took the «משוואת» prefix, the conic clause did not («משוואת הפרבולה I היא …» `not-handled`); no clause took a comma after the name; «הינה/הינו» were missing from `COPULA_WORDS`.
5. **The ambiguous-curve refusal taught a kite.** «P על הפרבולה» with two parabolas answered `ambiguous-shape`, whose remedy is «שטח הדלתון ABCD הוא 24».

**Decision.**
1. **`engine/names.ts` — one table** of every prefixed id kind (`line-`, `circle-`, `circle-at-`, `circle-thru-`, `parabola-`, `ellipse-`, anonymous `curve-`) → `RefKind` + the name the student wrote. `refKindOf`/`statedName` read it (re-exported from `apply.ts`, so no caller moved). The refusal TEXT moved out of `App.tsx` into `app/errorText.ts`, whose per-kind tables are `Record<RefKind, …>` — a new curve kind cannot reach a refusal without a noun (`errUnknownRefParabola`/`Ellipse` added).
2. **`classify` checks the claim** for every noun × every family, at the one place the family is decided: a fitted family other than the stated one is `kind-mismatch` with the `actual` family; the scope refusals (hyperbola, translated, rotated) keep precedence. `derive` reports it as its own fault code, and the student reads «המשוואה במשפט "…" מתארת מעגל, לא פרבולה» (`errKindMismatch`). This covers named and anonymous forms and lines too («נתון הישר l1: x^2+y^2=4»).
3. **`numeralCurveId(kind, numeral)`** is THE id of a numeral-named curve, canonical Roman (ADR-AG-168's policy, widened to parabolas and ellipses), used by the mint (every naming clause), the operand resolver, `curveByName`, `app/lines.ts` and the circle lookups in `apply.ts`. The LABEL keeps the student's own numeral («פרבולה 1»). The operator's 2026-09-21 ruling on #1257 (*a digit MAY name a line or a circle*) is unaffected: digits still name; they now name the SAME object as the Roman spelling, which is what ADR-AG-168 and #1257's measured plan already record for circles.
4. **One naming clause per language for circle, parabola and ellipse** (noun alternation), and **one connective grammar** (`NAMING_TAIL_HE`/`_EN`: comma · dash · «שמשוואתו» · copula · colon) shared with the line and centre-letter clauses; `NUMERAL_SEP` admits the comma; `COPULA_WORDS` gains «הינו/הינה/הינם/הינן» at every copula site. The English clause is no longer `i`-flagged (a lowercase `i`/`v` is not a numeral — the ADR-AG-006 trap).
5. **`ambiguous-curve`** — its own code and keys (`errAmbiguousCurve`, `errNoSuchCurve`; `errAmbiguousShape` is untouched, PR #1513 owns it). It carries the candidates as the student can write them (the name, or the equation of an unnamed curve) and the example is the student's own sentence with the first name inserted — «P על הפרבולה I» — locked to record. Emitted by `on-kind`, the contextual tangency and the diameter-of-a-circle lookups.

**Measured.** The sheet's nine red cases green through `decideSubmit` + `errorText`; 53 new locks in `issue-1271-1336-conic-naming.test.ts` (verb crossings × 4 curves; no raw id in any curve-kind refusal, He and En; the 4 × 4 noun × family matrix, named and anonymous; the numeral identity per kind with restatement and contradiction; 13 connective spellings; the ambiguous refusal's text and its taught example recording). Lock moves, each with its reason in the diff: `issue-1216` (`circle-1` → `circle-I`, name unchanged), `circle-centre` (a circle noun over a line equation is now `kind-mismatch`, not the downstream `does-not-exist`), and five `ambiguous-shape` → `ambiguous-curve` assertions (`onkind`, `tangency`, `issue-1429`, `issue-1464`).

**Deliberately not built.** (a), (b) — superseded by the operator's rulings, see Amendment 2. (c) R7's hyperbola wording («that is a hyperbola») is still the generic `out-of-scope` text. (d) The English «equation of the parabola I is …» prefix has no English clause (the Hebrew one is built). (e) `CENTRE_HE` («O מרכז מעגל 1») still reads only a letter — #1257 arm A.

### ADR-AG-170 Amendment 2 — 2026-09-29 operator rulings: «1» and «I» are one name for every curve, mixing is refused, a circle is the a = b ellipse

**Status:** accepted · 2026-09-29 · operator rulings on PR #1514 (`ruling-1514.md`, posted on the PR): *"so if user had line 1 and now want like I we refuse and ask to stick to a single notation."*

**Requirements:** [02c](02c-requirements-analytic.md) R51 (numeral names, rewritten), R7 (the ellipse/circle pair) · **Design:** [04c](04c-design-analytic.md) — the numeral paragraph (`numeralKey`/`numeralTwin`, one 1–9/I–IX table) and the `Curve.kind` paragraph (the a = b ellipse)

**Rulings.** (1) A digit and a Roman numeral are the SAME name for every named object — lines too. (2) MIXING the notations is refused with a note: once an object is named «1», naming or referring to it as «I» (or the reverse) is refused, the message says the two are one name and asks the student to keep the notation already in use. (3) An ellipse whose equation is a circle is accepted; every other noun/equation mismatch stays refused.

**What Amendment 1 had, and why it moved.** Am. 1 made the id the canonical Roman numeral, so «פרבולה 1» + «הפרבולה I» silently became one object. Ruling 2 forbids the silent merge — and a refusal that says "this figure writes it 1" needs the notation in use kept on the object. So the id now keeps the student's notation (`line-1`, `circle-I`) and identity across notations moved to `numeralKey`; `numeralCurveId` stays the one minting function.

**Decision.**
1. **One numeral table** in `engine/names.ts` (1–9 ↔ I–IX). Every numeral token of the grammar is built from it — `LINE_NUMERAL`, `CIRCLE_NUMERALS`, `CIRCLE_NUMERAL_RUN`, the noun-less Roman form, the operand resolver — so lines gain VI–IX and circles, parabolas and ellipses gain 6–9/VI–IX. The separator lookahead still keeps a coefficient («המעגל 4x^2…») from being read as a name; two digits are not a name.
2. **The mix refusal at the chokepoint, not per rule.** `numeralTwin(ids, id)` finds an object named by the same numeral in the other notation. `apply.ts` asks it where a numeral name MEETS the figure: at the top of `applyFact` for a NEW `curve`/`circle-thru`/`line-at` id (naming), and inside `unknownRef` (every reference that fails to resolve — point-on, crossings, relations, «O מרכז המעגל I», tangency, diameter, English). The result is `numeral-notation` with `detail` = the numeral typed, `holder` = the one in use, `expected` = the kind; the student reads «ישר 1 וישר I הם אותו שם — הכלי קורא ספרה ומספר רומי כשם אחד. כדי לא לערבב שתי כתיבות, כתבו ישר 1, כמו בשורות הקודמות.» (`errNumeralNotation`, He + En). The ask lane's missing-name answer carries the notation in use too (`missingCurve`, `askNumeralNotation`), so «משוואת הישר I» asked of «ישר 1» gets the same note, not "no such line".
3. **The a = b ellipse.** `classify(k, 'ellipse')` over a circle centred at the origin returns `{kind: 'ellipse', a: r, b: r}` — the object IS the student's ellipse: its name, «P על האליפסה I», the contextual «P על האליפסה», crossings and `curveKindOf` all see an ellipse. Its foci: `ellipseFoci` gives c = √(a²−b²) = 0, so **both foci coincide at the centre** (chosen over "one focus": the exam's F₁, F₂ pair keeps its shape). An off-centre circle under the ellipse noun is a translated ellipse — `out-of-scope`, as any translated ellipse is.

**Measured.** 128 new lock cases in `issue-1271-1336-conic-naming.test.ts`: for each of the four kinds × five numeral pairs × both directions — the same notation keeps working, a REFERENCE in the other notation is refused with the note (He and En text asserted), a second NAMING in the other notation is refused; the neighbour shapes (crossing, parallel relation, centre, English, a crossing with a parabola) reach the same refusal; the ask lane; VII names a line; the ellipse/circle pair records in four spellings as `{ellipse, a = b}`, is referable and crossable, its foci coincide, and the other mismatches stay refused. Lock moves: `issue-1216` (ids back to `circle-1`; the closed range is now 10, with 9 and IX accepted), `issue-1429` («P על המעגל 1» beside circle I is now the notation refusal — this supersedes ADR-AG-168's digit-onto-Roman reading).

**Deliberately not built.** The ask lane's note cannot know the noun (the question's name slot carries none), so «משוואת המעגל I» asked of a figure whose only «1» is a LINE gets the notation note rather than "no such circle".

### ADR-AG-170 Amendment 3 — 2026-09-29 merge with #1511 (circle tangency) and #1513 (measure roles): one host seam, one naming chokepoint

**Status:** accepted · 2026-09-29 · the merge of `main` @ `2604dcf2` after the operator approved all five PRs.

**Requirements:** none (internal — no promise changes; the three features keep their behaviour) · **Design:** [04c](04c-design-analytic.md) — the numeral paragraph (the circle subject reads numerals) and the host seam

**Decision.**
1. **One host-refusal mechanism.** This PR's `ambiguous-curve` code is folded into #1513's `ambiguous-shape` + `HostRef`: `noHost(src, kind, found)` accepts the FOUND OBJECTS, and when several named curves are found the host carries how to call each (`HostRef.candidates`). `hostKey` stays the one chooser for refusal and ask: `errHost.<none|many|pair>.<kind>` as #1513 built it, plus `errHost.named` (this PR's sentence that names the candidates and shows the student's own line with the first name) when candidates are present. Candidates are passed only where the sentence form reads a name back (point-on, contextual tangency, diameter, `radius-of`); `focus-of`/`directrix` keep #1513's kind-specific remedy, because «F מוקד הפרבולה I» does not parse and a taught remedy must record. This PR's `errNoSuchCurve` is dropped: #1513's `errHost.none.<kind>` says the same, per kind. The refusal TEXT stays in `app/errorText.ts`, which now also renders #1513's `out-of-domain` (`rangeText`); `HOST_KINDS` is exhaustive over `HostRef['kind']` and a lock checks every kind × arity key in both locales.
2. **One naming chokepoint.** #1511's and #1513's new circle-name lookups (`radius-of`, `tangent-circles`, the radius ask) go through `numeralCurveId` and the twin-aware `unknownRef`, so «רדיוס המעגל I» of «מעגל 1», given or asked, gets the notation note. #1511's circle SUBJECT reader read a numeral as a CENTRE letter («המעגלים I ו-II משיקים» minted a point «I» and a second circle); a numeral subject is now a reference to the named circle (`SUBJECT_NUMERAL`, `isNumeralName`), so the notation rule holds there too, and «מעגל 1 ומעגל II משיקים» — `not-handled` on `main` — is understood (and refused `out-of-scope` for equation circles, as the pair form already was). The bare «נתון מעגל I» keeps its current reading (#1257 arm B, not built).
3. **The a = b ellipse and #1513's roles.** «מוקדי האליפסה» answers «(0, 0), (0, 0)» for it; `kind-mismatch` sits in `classify`, before any role, so a role on a mismatched conic is never reached (the line is refused first).

**Behaviour change.** «המעגל I משיק לציר ה-x» on an empty canvas no longer creates a circle centred at a new point I; it refers to circle I and is refused as unknown when there is none (the 2026-09-19 ruling: «I» names the circle, it does not name a centre).

**Measured.** 7 merge locks in `issue-1271-1336-conic-naming.test.ts`; the #1511 and #1513 sheets replayed on the merged server.

## ADR-AG-172 — The fallback teaches the session's language: a one-locale prompt, and rows that show the student's own sentence (#1297)

**Status:** accepted · 2026-09-28 · operator rulings 2026-09-24 (*"nothing should be in english if data was entered in hebrew"*) and 2026-09-27 (*"student's words now, form later"* — the proper-form-beside split to #1468) · round #1510. Numbered 172 beside the round's parallel branches.

**Requirements:** [02c](02c-requirements-analytic.md) R104 family (the escape's promise) · **Design:** [04c](04c-design-analytic.md) fallback

**Context.** One Hebrew sentence, escalated; the model wrote three English canonical rows into a Hebrew session's fact list — valid, parsed, committed, and taught. The language of the recorded line was the one thing in the lane still resting on prompt discipline (one soft sentence), which #1251's own ADR argues safety must never do.

**Decision.** Two structural changes. (1) **The prompt speaks one language**: the client sends its session `locale`; the shared harness (`buildSystemPrompt`) renders ONE vocabulary column and a HARD language rule for it; analytic's `vocabulary(locale)` implements the column; an old caller (no locale — 2-D/3-D today) keeps its prompt byte-identical, so the sibling byte-identity locks stand. The proxy widens (`parseHandler` reads `body.locale`), which makes this a proxy deploy. (2) **No model output is ever displayed as a row**: the store gains `spokenFor` — per line index, the student's own sentence — written by `recordLlmLines`, index-maintained through remove/edit (an edited row shows the editor's text), persisted in the save envelope as an optional field (old files restore clean), and the fact panel displays it over the machine line. The machine lines stay the stored truth: **replay is pure over the lines exactly as before** — which is why the sentence is an annotation and not the stored line (the student's refused sentence cannot replay; that is what the fallback was for).

**Measured.** 6 locks (`issue-1297-hebrew-fact.test.ts` product-side; `issue-1297-locale-prompt.test.ts` server-side, on the sanctioned import direction): the He prompt carries only the He column + the hard rule, the En prompt only En, the no-locale prompt byte-compatible; rows display the sentence with part markers, annotations follow their lines through removal, drop on edit, and survive save→restore.

**Consequences.** `server/llm/harness.ts` (locale through `PromptSpec.vocabulary`/`buildSystemPrompt`/`buildRequest`), `server/parseHandler.ts` (`body.locale`), `parser/llmSharedAnalytic.ts` (one-column vocab), `parser/llmAnalytic.ts` + `App.tsx` (locale sent; `recordLlmLines`; row display), `store/useAnalyticStore.ts` (`spokenFor` + envelope field). **Proxy redeploy required.**

## ADR-AG-176 — «זווית BMC» is askable: the angle ask arm, with the ruled working (#1409)

**Status:** accepted · 2026-09-28 · operator 2026-09-24 (*"in data panel, i cannot ask for זווית BMC"*), trace method ruled 2026-09-27 (*"if its an angle where m=tanx would work, use that, if not, use law of cosine"*) · round #1517. Numbered 176 beside the round's parallel branches.

**Requirements:** [02c](02c-requirements-analytic.md) R121 (new) · **Design:** [04c](04c-design-analytic.md) — the ask lane's shared atoms

**Context.** #1331 (ADR-AG-153) made the three-letter angle a GIVEN through the parser's own atoms; it added no ask arm, and nothing checked sayable ⇒ askable — the two surfaces drifted apart the first time a measure shipped without its twin. Re-measured at pickup: every angle spelling still `unreadable`.

**Decision.** (1) `readAngleAsk` (parser) — the ask reference composed from the SAME atoms the given rules read (`ANGLE_NOUN_HE/EN` + `ANGLE_LETTERS`, plus the ask's optional «גודל» lead-in), so every spelling the given accepts is askable by construction; three letters only (a lone vertex needs the figure, #1407 — out of the ask's scope for now). (2) The value comes from the SAME `angleAt` the angle residual constrains (exported from `engine/solve.ts`) — «זווית ABC = 60» asked back prints exactly 60° (locked) — through `isKnowledge` like every value arm: open answers open, a missing letter gets #1111's outcome, formatted by the one `angleText`. (3) The WORKING per the ruling: `traceAngle` (`engine/techniques.ts`) — the slope method where both arms have a defined slope and 1 + m₁m₂ ≠ 0, with the «180° − α» row when obtuse; else the law of cosines with the three lengths; each branch's trace ends on the answer (locked per branch). (4) The sayable ⇒ askable CLASS GUARD: a curated walk over every value measure (length, area, point-line distance, slope, x-axis angle, angle) asserting none is `unreadable` on a determined figure — a new value measure joins the list in its own commit, which is the review point #1331 never had. The ask placeholder teaches «זווית ABC».

**Deviations from the plan.** The plan's step 5 wanted the guard to WALK the catalog mechanically; the shipped guard is a curated list (the catalog rows do not machine-map to ask spellings), which holds the same line at the cost of one list entry per new measure — recorded here as the trade.

**Consequences.** `src-analytic/parser/parseAnalytic.ts` (`readAngleAsk`), `src-analytic/engine/solve.ts` (`angleAt` exported), `src-analytic/engine/techniques.ts` (`traceAngle`), `src-analytic/app/ask.ts` (the arm), `src-analytic/i18n/index.ts` (placeholder), docs 02c R121. Lock: `issue-1409-angle-ask.test.ts` — every reported spelling, the honesty gates, the 60° round trip, the four trace branches ending on the answer, and the class guard.

### ADR-AG-176 Am. 1 — a method hint replaces the worked angle trace (#1525)

**Status:** accepted · 2026-09-29 · operator, playing round #1517 T26 on this PR: «tan α = |(m₁ - m₂)/(1 + m₁·m₂)| … this equation is not in the curriculum. I think we should not try to show the process … maybe just write a comment "ניתן להשתמש בשיפועי הישרים או במשפט הקוסינוסים" the part about the cosine law should show only if all 3 nodes are known.» Approved as #1525 the same day. **Reverses** the 2026-09-27 trace ruling this ADR was built on.

**Requirements:** docs/02c R121 (amended) · **Design:** none (internal — the ask lane's answer gains a `hint` token, as `fact` did)

**Decision.** The angle arm returns no `trace`. It returns a `hint` token instead: `angle-methods` when all three vertices are knowledge (both coordinates fixed across configurations, the same `isKnowledge` gate the answer passes), else `angle-slopes`, since the law of cosines needs the three lengths. The component words it through the locale (He «ניתן להשתמש בשיפועי הישרים או במשפט הקוסינוסים» / «ניתן להשתמש בשיפועי הישרים»; En mirrors), below the answer. `traceAngle` is deleted, not left unused. **A stated angle gets no hint** (operator, T33, same day: «if the angle is given in the input, there is no point explaining how to find it»): when a stated angle given exists at the asked vertex between the same two arms, in either order (the `angle` constraint the given lowers to), the answer is the value alone. The check reads the record, not the number, so a computed angle that equals a stated number keeps its hint.

**Measured.** His case A(0,0), B(4,0), C(8,4), «זווית ABC»: 135°, the full hint, and no formula rows (driven on the PR server and read). An angle the givens fix while a vertex stays free (B, C, «משולש ABC», «זווית ABC = 60»): 60° with the slopes-only hint.

**Consequences.** `src-analytic/app/ask.ts`, `src-analytic/App.tsx`, `src-analytic/i18n/index.ts`, `src-analytic/engine/techniques.ts` (`traceAngle` removed). Lock: `issue-1409-angle-ask.test.ts`, whose "ruled working" block is replaced by the hint cases.

## ADR-AG-173 — A refusal about a reused letter names the letter, and its defining sentence (#1423)

**Status:** accepted · 2026-09-28 · operator, playing round #1408 (T41: *"there is a refusal but there is an intersect to select"*) · round #1517

**Requirements:** [02c](02c-requirements-analytic.md) — the honesty invariant for refusals (a refusal names the conflicting statement) · **Design:** [04c](04c-design-analytic.md) — the submit verdict's context fields

**Context.** His P was already the second crossing of AB. By the #1046 lowering a line reusing an existing letter is a STATEMENT about that point, so «P נקודת החיתוך … של הצלע CA» asserts something false and is rightly refused — but the refusal said only «לא נמצאה תצורה שבה מתקיים: "P …"», naming the new line alone, beside a visibly free crossing. Re-measured at pickup (tip `d3f08a4c`): the issue's whole table stood — the fresh letter records, and the three P-reuse statement kinds (crossing, coordinates, midpoint) all refuse with `unsatisfiable` + the new line only.

**Decision.** At the ONE submit chokepoint (`app/submit.ts`, the fault return every typed line passes), a refused line whose SUBJECT id already exists gains `reusedId` + `definedBy` — the id, and the student's own earliest line that introduces it (`subjectIdsOf` over the parsed facts: placed points, derived points, declarations, on-object riders; polygon vertices count as introducers for the definer scan). Decided structurally, never by sentence kind, so every point sentence — present and future — gets it. The App renders the reused wording: «P כבר מוגדרת: "…". המשפט "…" סותר את ההגדרה הקיימת — לנקודה חדשה בחרו אות אחרת» (`errUnsatisfiableReused`, both locales). The engine's refusal itself is unchanged (the logic was always right; the message was not).

**Measured.** The operator's exact canvas (from `logs/debug-log-analytic.jsonl`, session `m49ph672`): both his refused lines now carry `reusedId: P` + `definedBy` = his own AB-crossing sentence; so do «P(1,1)» and «P אמצע AC» (the class). The taught remedy drives: «S …» records. Neighbours held: a TRUE reused-letter statement stays absorbed (#1046), `crossing-already-named` keeps its own holder-naming refusal (ADR-AG-157).

**Consequences.** `src-analytic/app/submit.ts` (`subjectIdsOf`, `definingLineOf`, the enriched fault return), `src-analytic/store/useAnalyticStore.ts` (the `unsatisfiable` variant's optional fields), `src-analytic/App.tsx` (key pick), `src-analytic/i18n/index.ts` (`errUnsatisfiableReused`, he+en). Lock: `issue-1423-reused-letter.test.ts` — his exact sequence, the class (coordinates, midpoint), the driving remedy, and the three neighbours.

## ADR-AG-174 — «הנקודה» is optional in the distance grammar, and the contextual form resolves by rewrite (#1431)

**Status:** accepted · 2026-09-28 · external prod review relayed by the operator (2026-09-27) · round #1517. Numbered 174 beside the round's parallel branch (173 = #1423).

**Requirements:** [02c](02c-requirements-analytic.md) — ask/given parity for a spelling · **Design:** [04c](04c-design-analytic.md) — the one measure-term atom

**Context.** «המרחק של הנקודה A מהישר l1» was unreadable as an ask and not-handled as a given while «המרחק של A מהישר l1» answered 4 — the optional-subject-noun trap (`הנקודה A ≡ A`, the #1134/#1151 shape); «מרחק A מ-l1» (construct state) was unreadable too. Re-measured at pickup: the issue's table stood.

**Decision.** (1) The `NOUN` slot of the ONE distance atom (`engine/lengths.ts`, the #1151 frames) gains the point nouns («נקודה», «קדקוד», En "point"), so the ask and the given read the spelling by construction — no per-surface copy. (2) The construct state joins as a fourth frame (empty opener; the «מ-» join still required, so a bare «מרחק AB» length is never claimed). (3) The ruled contextual form («המרחק של הנקודה מהישר», no letters — operator 2026-09-27): answers exactly when the figure holds ONE point and ONE line, by REWRITING into the lettered sentence at the ask entry and falling through to the one distance lane (the ADR-W-053 synonym rule the symbolic d_{AB} spellings follow); otherwise a new `contextual` answer field carries the counts and the App names the ambiguity — never «לא הבנתי».

**Consequences.** `src-analytic/engine/lengths.ts` (`NOUN`, the construct frame), `src-analytic/app/ask.ts` (the contextual rewrite + `Answer.contextual`), `src-analytic/App.tsx` + `src-analytic/i18n/index.ts` (the ambiguity wording, he+en). Lock: `issue-1431-distance-noun.test.ts` — every reported spelling × both surfaces, the contextual answer and its two-point refusal, the bare-pair control.

## ADR-AG-175 — Every ask arm consults the option set, by calling the panel's decision (#1433)

**Status:** accepted · 2026-09-28 · external prod review relayed by the operator (2026-09-27) · round #1517. Numbered 175 beside the round's parallel branches (173 = #1423, 174 = #1431).

**Requirements:** [02c](02c-requirements-analytic.md) — «cannot be computed» must never stand beside a panel that lists the options · **Design:** [04c](04c-design-analytic.md) — one knowledge decision per surface pair

**Context.** With two valid configurations, asking «C» answered «לא ניתן לחשב מהנתונים» while the panel listed both of C's positions; «AC» and «משוואת הישר AC» likewise. #1227 (ADR-AG-136) fixed this false absence for the locus question only. Class: *each ask arm owned its own knowledge gate.* Re-measured at pickup: the issue's whole table stood.

**Decision.** (1) The panel's point decision is EXTRACTED to `app/pointText.ts` — value → #1036 option set (drawn one bracketed) → #1226 stated expression → #1023 line dependency → half-pinned → open dash — and the ask's point arm now CALLS it, so the two surfaces answer the same text by construction (the #1102 locks-must-call rule). (2) One scalar option gate (`scalarText`): a value when forced, else the resolution-aware set joined «או», else null; the measure arm and the slope arm ride it. (3) The equation arm answers its option set deduped by the RENDERED equation (coefficients are homogeneous, so raw triples may differ for one line); a set collapsing to one text stays null — a single «option» would claim what the knowledge gate withheld. `askNoValue` is thereby reserved for a figure that determines nothing finite.

**Measured.** The reported figure: «C» → «[(1, -5)] או (3, 3)», «AC» → «3.16 או 5.83», the equation → both equations. Controls: a free point stays open; a determined figure answers its single value with no «או».

**Consequences.** `src-analytic/app/pointText.ts` (new — the extracted decision + `scalarText`), `src-analytic/app/ask.ts` (point/slope/equation/measure arms), `src-analytic/App.tsx` (imports the moved decision). Lock: `issue-1433-known-options.test.ts` — the reported rows, the surfaces-agree assertion (calling, not reproducing), and the two gates that must not loosen.

## ADR-AG-177 — A given can be MUTED: the fact list's third D6 operation (#1548)

**Status:** accepted · 2026-09-29 · operator: *"2d, 3d, and complex have the checkbox on the input line that allows to disable that input but analytics doesnt and should"*

**Requirements:** [02c](02c-requirements-analytic.md) R81 — the givens list offers the suite's three row operations · **Design:** [04c](04c-design-analytic.md) — the active projection, and the `toggle` log action

**Context.** [docs/28](28-product-unification.md) D6 ruled *disable, edit in place and delete — all three, in every builder*, and B5 (#670) built the shared chrome (`shell/frame/FactList.tsx`) that renders each control only when the product passes its handler. This builder joined after B5 and mounted the chrome with `onEditCommit` and `onDelete` only; its store held `lines` and nothing else, so the chrome — correctly — drew no checkbox. Nothing in the suite checked that every builder passes all three, which is how the gap shipped.

**Decision.** (1) The store gains `disabled: number[]` — indexes into `lines`, complex's shape. It rides the undo history (a mute is a step), the save file (`disabled`, omitted when empty, so older saves are unchanged), the session persistence and the share link; `removeLine` shifts it, `clearAll` empties it, `restore` range-checks it. (2) **The ACTIVE projection** (`app/active.ts`: `activeOf`, `rowOf`): the figure is derived from the unmuted lines, and every consumer that took "the lines" — `derive`, `decideSubmit`, the fallback, «הציגו תצורה אחרת», the ask lane — now takes the active list and needs no knowledge of muting (to each of them a muted line was never said). Only the fact list shows the whole list, and `rowOf` translates a derivation's per-line results (faults, tool-chosen names) back to rows. The engine is untouched. (3) **The gates, per D6 rulings (a) and (b):** muting always applies — a dependent line then faults on its OWN row, reversibly (this builder's rows carry their own status, the 3-D shape); **un-muting** faces the typed-line gate (`decideToggle`): the line returns at its position, and if it faults or a fault APPEARS that was not there before (compared by sentence and code, since later active indexes shift), the row stays muted and the refusal names the line — `decideSubmit`'s #1334 rule for a line that is not last. **Editing a muted row** rewrites text only, but it must still parse (`decideEdit`, extracted from `App.tsx` so its lock calls it). (4) The load audit replays the figure the student will see (active lines, faults mapped to rows) and also names a MUTED line that no longer parses — it would be refused on un-mute, and the drift net exists for exactly that.

**The class.** *A builder mounts the shared fact list without one of the three handlers, and the chrome's "no handler, no control" rule makes the gap invisible.* Closed suite-wide by `shell/__tests__/fact-list-ops-parity-1548.test.ts`: every builder's `<FactList>` must pass `onToggle`, `onEditCommit` and `onDelete` (a brace-depth scan of the element's own props, so a row's `chip.onToggle` cannot satisfy it), with an explicit `EXEMPT` table for a stated exception. Measured on `main`: it fails for analytic alone.

**Consequences.** `src-analytic/app/active.ts` (new), `src-analytic/app/submit.ts` (`decideToggle`, `decideEdit`), `src-analytic/store/useAnalyticStore.ts`, `src-analytic/app/loadSession.ts`, `src-analytic/app/sessionPersistAn.ts`, `src-analytic/App.tsx` (the active projection, the row map, `onToggle`), `src-analytic/i18n/index.ts` (`factToggle`, the complex wording). Dev-only triage replay treats a `toggle` action as `degraded`, its stated rule for an action it does not model. Locks: `src-analytic/__tests__/fact-ops-1548.test.ts` (13 — mute/un-mute figure, the dependent's own-row fault, the refused un-mute naming its line, muted and active edits, remove-shift, undo, clear, save/load/audit, malformed indexes) + the suite lock above.

## ADR-AG-178 — The freedom count ranks equation rows only; a one-sided bound is tagged at its producer (#1556)

**Status:** accepted · 2026-09-29 · found triaging #1554 (operator session) · round #1559

**Requirements:** none (internal) — restores [02c](02c-requirements-analytic.md) R22 (the freedom cue) and the honesty invariant that a stated given never vanishes · **Design:** [04c](04c-design-analytic.md) — the tangency section: the extent rows are bounds, and the count does not rank them

**Context.** A tangential quadrilateral typed one side per line — «מרובע ABCD», then «מעגל M משיק לצלע AB / BC / CD / DA». The fourth line answered «זה כבר נובע מהנתונים שכתבתם» and was dropped, while the drawn circle sat 2.300 from DA with radius 3.249. The entailment gate (`decideSubmit`, #1063) reads "trial holds, nothing gained, freedom unchanged" as entailment, and the freedom read `carrierDof` 8, 10, 9, **7**, 7 — the third tangency removed two.

**Measured (step 1 of the plan; the plan's hypothesis CONFIRMED).** Residual rows and the central-difference J at seed 0 of the four-line figure: 11 unknowns, nine rows (three tangencies × [distance, `max(0,−t)·n`, `max(0,t−1)·n`], #1503). The solved vector parks CD's touch point exactly at D (t = 1); that constraint's upper hinge has residual 0 and a non-zero J row (the difference straddles the kink — a half-slope), so rank(J) = 4 for three equations. At the same vector, the two other bounded rows are inactive (zero rows). Before, line 5 answered `already-follows` at 11/24 seeds.

**The class.** *A one-sided residual row (an admissibility bound) is ranked by the freedom count as if it were an equation.* Two producers exist in this tree, both `max(0, …)` hinges: the bounded side of a tangency (#1503) and the bounded crossing (#1286). Grepped every `Math.max(0` in `residual`: those two, nothing else; the concentric floor of circle tangency (#1504) is one row that stays an equation. This is ADR-AG-005 D7 at row level — a domain/selector/bound is not a constraint on the dimension of the solution set.

**Decision.** At the producer: `residual` becomes `residualRows`, returning `{ eq, bound? }` from every arm; the two hinge arms return their rows as `bound`. `residual` (the solve's input) concatenates them in the old order, so the solve is byte-for-byte unchanged; `equalityResidual` returns `eq` alone. `CarrierSystem` gains `equalitiesAt`, and `figureDofOf` hands only that to `freeRank` (whose parameter is now named `equalities` and documented as such). No consumer has to know which arm emits a clamp; a new bounded arm declares its kind where it is written. **The locus walk keeps the full rows** (`nullDirection` over `residualsAt`), deliberately: for a walk a bound at its kink is where the trace should end, so there it is information, not a phantom.

**Measured after.** `carrierDof` 8, 10, 9, 8, 7 (and the same in reverse entry order); line 5 → `record` at 24/24 seeds; with all five lines DA is tangent and the figure whole at 24/24. 24-seed whole-rate before/after — the reported figure 24/24 → 24/24 (2 distinct configurations either way), the four-line prefix 24/24 → 24/24, the control (a triangle's incircle side by side) 24/24 → 24/24, 5 distinct, `carrierDof` 6 either way. Per-derive cost of the reported figure ~130 → ~150 ms, run-to-run noise: the count makes the same number of residual passes, over fewer rows. «הציגו תצורה אחרת» moves the figure (0 → 11 → 26 → 42, `found: true` each) before and after — the #1282 second consumer (`isKnowledge`/`drawableAt`) does not read the count's value beyond `carrierDof === 0`, which this figure never is.

**Found, not fixed here.** The raw solve of a bounded-side tangential quadrilateral is whole at only 1/24 seeds (`evaluate`, before `drawableAt`'s walk) — which is why seeds 0–10 show one configuration: the walk carries them all to seed 10. The count fix does not touch that; it is a solve-quality question for its own issue.

**Sibling audit.** 2-D (`src/engine/dofRank.ts`) already excludes order constraints from its rank (`isOrderConstraint`), at constraint granularity — the same principle; class absent. 3-D (`src3d/engine/solve3.ts` `numericRank`) ranks no hinge rows; class absent. Complex has no freedom rank.

**Consequences.** `src-analytic/engine/solve.ts` (`residualRows`, `ResidualRows`, `residual`/`equalityResidual`, `freeRank`'s contract), `src-analytic/engine/evaluate.ts` (`CarrierSystem.equalitiesAt`, `figureDofOf`). Lock: `src-analytic/__tests__/issue-1556-freerank-equality-rows.test.ts` — both hinge producers at their kink (one `eq` row, ranked alone, and the phantom shown on the full rows), the operator's five lines through the real gate at 24 seeds, the 8-10-9-8-7 count in both entry orders, DA tangent and whole at 24 seeds, ≥ 2 configurations and «הציגו תצורה אחרת» moving, the incircle control, and the entailment guards (#1063's area; a bounded tangency restated in the other letter order).

## ADR-AG-179 — A numeral name means one curve at every site that reads it: the centre slot, the ring words and the line ids join `names.ts` (#1529)

**Status:** accepted · 2026-09-29 · operator approval of the six P1s ("approve them and fix") · round #1559.

**Requirements:** [02c](02c-requirements-analytic.md) R90 — «O מרכז מעגל 1» and every numeral the circle was named by; every offered ring on a numeral-named curve records · **Design:** [04c](04c-design-analytic.md) — the numeral paragraph (`lineIdOf`, the reverse direction, the guard)

**Context.** Reported while measuring #1257: «נתון מעגל 1 שמשוואתו x^2+y^2=9 · נתון מעגל I שמשוואתו x^2+y^2=16 · P על מעגל 1» put P on the r = 4 circle, drawn green — the mint wrote `circle-1`, the reference (#1429) looked up `circle-I`. The plan ("Part A" of #1257) asked for one numeral→id function at the ~12 sites, with the id Roman per ADR-AG-168.

**Re-measured at pickup (tip `5f6a66d3`).** The reported symptom was already gone: PR #1514 (ADR-AG-170 Am. 1–3) moved every circle and conic site onto `numeralCurveId`, and the operator's 2026-09-29 ruling on that PR **superseded the Roman-id policy**: the id keeps the student's notation and MIXING is refused. The reported sequence now refuses line 2 (`numeral-notation`, «מעגל 1 ומעגל I הם אותו שם…») and P sits on the r = 3 circle; «P על מעגל 1» after a digit declaration records. This ADR follows that ruling, not the plan's "the id is Roman". What the measurement still found, all the same class (*a numeral name known at one site and not at its neighbour*):
1. **The centre rule's circle slot read `NAME`** (a capital letter): «O מרכז מעגל I» worked by the accident of I being a letter, while «O מרכז מעגל 1», «O מרכז המעגל II» and "O is the centre of circle 2" were `not-handled` — the ninth site the plan listed (`CENTRE_HE`/`EN`), untouched by #1514.
2. **`centresOf` OFFERED those sentences as rings**, so the centre ring of a digit- or II–IX-named circle was a click that failed (ADR-AG-054).
3. **`crossings.ts` composed a named curve's words from its LABEL** and knew only the Roman circles I–V (`/^(I|II|III|IV|V)$/`, a hand copy of the numeral table): a label now carries its noun («ישר 1», «פרבולה I», "circle 1"), so every crossing ring on a numeral-named line, parabola or ellipse wrote «הישר ישר 1» / «הישר פרבולה I» and was refused `bad-operand`.
4. **Line-name ids were spelled `line-${…}` at eight sites** (parser ×7, `apply.ts`, `curveByName` ×2, `app/lines.ts`) — identical strings today, but the copies the #1529 shape grows from.

**Decision.**
1. `names.ts` gains `lineIdOf(name)` (= `numeralCurveId('line', name)`); every line-name id goes through it. **No site outside `names.ts` spells a `line-`/`circle-`/`parabola-`/`ellipse-` id** — enforced by a source guard.
2. The centre rule reads `(?:ה?מעגל\s+)?(NAME) | ה?מעגל\s+(NUMERAL_ALT)` — NAME first, so a single capital keeps its reading and id; a numeral only after the noun (#1298); the English twin is `i`-flagged for its words, so its numeral is re-checked case-sensitively (`isNumeralName`) and a lowercase «ii» is refused, never built (ADR-AG-006).
3. A numeral-named curve's words come from its id: `CONIC_NOUN[refKindOf(id)] + statedName(id)` («הישר 1», «הפרבולה I», «המעגל 2»); `centresOf` selects its circles with `numeralKey` rather than slicing a `circle-` prefix (which would have read `circle-at-O` as «at-O»).

**Measured.** `issue-1529-numeral-ids.test.ts`, 27 cases: the reported sequence (the notation refusal on line 2, one circle, |P| = 3 at seeds 0–2); four «P על מעגל n» spellings; seven centre spellings (He/En, 1, 2, 9, I, II, IV) placing O at the fitted centre (1, 2), the notation note, the lowercase and noun-less refusals, the single-capital control; every ring `offersOf` gives on six numeral-named figures round-trips with zero faults; the source guard. 13 of the 27 fail on the pre-change tree. Related suites (conic naming, #1216, #1429, crossings/centres/rings, parser, catalogue — 37 files, 895 cases) green.

**Deliberately not built.** #1257's arms B–D (the bare «נתון מעגל 1» open circle, tangency on a curve host, refinement) — still that issue's feature PR; only Part A was this item.

## ADR-AG-180 — One configuration pool for every knowledge gate, completed after the render (#1473, P1)

**Status:** accepted · 2026-09-29 · measured on our own test figure; operator rulings 2026-09-29 (*"we cannot afford 0.5 s addition"*, then option **B′**: check after render, «בודק…» never a provisional number, the conic memo in the same change) · round #1559

**Requirements:** [02c](02c-requirements-analytic.md) R16 — "invariant across every admissible configuration" is judged over the full configuration pool; a value not yet confirmed shows «בודק…», never a number · **Design:** [04c](04c-design-analytic.md) — "One configuration pool, completed after the render" (under the ADR-AG-126 section), and the conic memo

**Amends** [ADR-AG-126](#adr-ag-126) (the #1282 note: `distinctConfigSeeds` stops being the knowledge gate's sample) and [ADR-AG-136](#adr-ag-136) (the resolution arm is scaled by the figure, as `SOLVE_RESOLUTION` is defined). **Cross-cites** [ADR-CX-049](06d-decisions-complex.md#adr-cx-049) (complex, #1427) and #1474 (3-D): the same rule — *knowledge is a comparison across the whole configuration set* — in trees that share no code.

**Context.** The panel printed `C = (x_C, −4)` for «משולש ABC · A(0,0) · B(6,0) · שטח המשולש ABC הוא 12» while «הציגו תצורה אחרת» drew C at y = +4; «C על הישר x=1 · שטח ABC = 6» plus an unrelated «נקודה Z» printed `(1, −3)` alone; a circle's crossing with the x-axis printed `(0, 0)` once «Q נמצאת על המעגל I» was added; and a line through that crossing printed `x = 0`. Re-measured at pickup (`5f6a66d3`): all four reproduced, and the ask lane answered the same wrong text. Corpus sweep (the #1289 corpus, 48-seed truth): 8 lies in 3 figures as-is, 13 in 7 with «נקודה Z». **Class: a knowledge gate reads a sample sized for "does it vary?" and treats it as the complete configuration set.** `isKnowledge` read three *distinct* configurations — any continuous DOF makes every seed distinct, so all three were spent on the continuous family and the discrete root was never varied; `knownCurve` read raw seeds 0–2; `knownOptions` read 24. Three gates, three pools.

**Decision.**
1. **`configurationPool(c)`** (`engine/evaluate.ts`): the drawable figures at seeds `0..POOL_SIZE−1` (24 — `knownOptions`' measured budget), one per construction (WeakMap), filled lazily and sharing `drawableAt`'s per-seed cache. `isKnowledge`'s default sample, `knownCurve`'s default (was `[0, 1, 2]`) and `knownOptions`' walk all read it, so "the value" and "the option set" are two readings of one set. `distinctConfigSeeds` keeps its API and remains what «תצורה אחרת» walks.
2. **Off the page, the first gate FILLS the pool** and answers the settled verdict — every test, lock and non-render caller.
3. **On the page (B′), the pool completes after the render.** `App.tsx` defers the pool of the derivation it renders. A deferred gate first pays the synchronous floor the render always paid (the distinct walk), then judges only the seeds already evaluated: a value those seeds already see differ is open at once (a superset can only widen it); one they read as invariant is **pending** (`{ known: false, pending: true }`). `knownOptions` on a value that has so far taken two values fills the pool — the walk the render paid before — and one that has taken one value is pending, spending nothing. Every pending answer reports to a `settled(fn)` probe, so a row composed from several gates (the ask lane's dozen arms, wrapped once in `askSettled`; a point row) shows «בודק…» (`checking`, He/En) and never a provisional number. `app/poolScheduler.ts` completes the pool one seed per slice, **yielding** to the browser between seeds (`scheduler.postTask`, else a `MessageChannel` message, else `setTimeout(0)` — never `requestIdleCallback`, see *Amendment 1*), from a **layout** effect keyed on the derivation — so a pool the render's own option walk completed settles before paint, with no «בודק…» flash — and its cleanup abandons the loop when the figure changes: the old pool is never advanced again and its completion never lands on the new figure.
4. **The resolution arm is scaled by the figure** (amending ADR-AG-136): `spread ≤ SOLVE_RESOLUTION · max(value scale, smallest figure span over the configurations read)`. `SOLVE_RESOLUTION` is defined relative to the figure's scale, and the arm scaled by the value; three samples hid it, the pool exposed it on #1259's own tangency (M = (4, 0): y lands in ±0.0018 over 24 seeds — 4.6e-4 of the span of 8, but 1.16× the resolution of a value of magnitude ~0). The SMALLEST span, so one seed that flings a free point out cannot widen the bar. Over the corpus (6862 coordinates, ±Z) it changes 0 verdicts beyond that figure.
5. **The conic memo** (`engine/conic.ts` `curveFromEquation`): pure over (the `Expr`, the exact values of the symbols it reads — `-0` kept apart from `0` — and the expected kind), memoised weakly per `Expr` (capped at 512 keys), results frozen because they are now shared (no caller mutates one; checked). ~45% of evaluation time on the heaviest line was refitting parameter-free equations inside the finite-difference Jacobian.

**Deliberately not ported: #1427's `complete` flag.** Analytic has no CAS (ADR-AG-001 D1): every solution set is a multi-start sample, so "withhold unless proven complete" would withhold every value in the product. **The pool is sampled, not proven**: a root reached less than about once in 24 seeds can still hide (measured 0 such cases over 1154 figures; the widest reported split was 11/48). If it fires, the fix is exact per-object enumeration (as `crossings.ts meetConic` does for curve crossings), never a blanket withhold, and never a smaller pool (12 seeds still lied on the kite + circle).

**Measured** (vitest, this machine, the page's synchronous path per line — derive + `panelKnowledge` + point rows + `segmentKnowledge` + the scene's `knownCurve`; min of 2 cold runs; before = `5f6a66d3`):
- **572 exam**, lines 1–11: before 2/0/6/3/1/44/111/14/314/522/**126** ms; after 2/0/4/3/1/21/48/6/133/208/**55** ms. In the browser (below) line 11 («M אמצע AB») shows «בודק…» for ~0.4 s; lines 5 and 8 for a few tens of ms.
- **572 + Z** line 12: 1513 → 685 ms. **kite + circle** (circle last) worst line 1825 → 1203 ms; (+Z) 2020 → 1334 ms; (circle first) 1538 → 1004 ms. On every kite line the render's own walk completes the pool (settled before paint).
- **Blocking added: 0 ms on every line** (the operation-count lock); every line is faster than before, by the memo.
- Correctness: the corpus invariant (48-seed truth, ±Z) goes from 8 / 13 lies to **0 / 0**; the conic memo changes no corpus figure's signature.

**Consequences.** `src-analytic/engine/evaluate.ts` (`configurationPool`, `POOL_SIZE`, `settled`, `reportPending`, the `Knowledge` type, the gates' defaults, the resolution arm, `evaluateStats`), `src-analytic/engine/conic.ts` (the memo, `__setConicMemo`, `conicStats`), `src-analytic/app/panelRows.ts` (`PanelKnown` = `Knowledge`, curve `pending`, `segmentKnowledge` + `uniqueSegments` moved from `App.tsx`), `src-analytic/app/pointText.ts` (a pending coordinate never falls through to the half-pinned form), `src-analytic/app/lineAngle.ts` (passes pending), `src-analytic/app/ask.ts` (`askSettled`, `Answer.pending`), `src-analytic/app/poolScheduler.ts` (new), `src-analytic/App.tsx` (defer, the layout effect, «בודק…» on every row kind and the ask), `src-analytic/i18n/index.ts` (`checking`, He/En). Locks: `issue-1473-knowledge-pool.test.ts` (cases A–D settled, the controls — A(4,0), 572 k = 2 and line 3, the #1282 verdicts, a determined two-root figure — the pool's fill/defer contract, the scheduler's abandonment), `issue-1473-mid-pool-render.test.tsx` (the real `App` rendered mid-pool: «בודק…», no number, both locales through `studentFacingViolations`), `issue-1473-perf-budget.test.ts` (render path ≤ the pre-#1473 seed consumers on every line of seven heavy figures; ≤ 48 evaluations per construction and 0 after; conic fits ÷5; identity with the memo off), `issue-1473-pool-invariant.test.ts` (slow tier — the class invariant over the corpus ±Z, and the memo's corpus identity). `issue-1276-display-epsilon.test.ts`'s source lock reads `panelRows.ts` too, where the slope gate moved. **Landing order:** #1539 (the `-0` signature) lands with or after this, never before.

### ADR-AG-180 Am. 1 — the pool YIELDS between seeds; it never waits for idle (browser pre-play, round #1559)

**Requirements:** none (internal) — R16's promise is unchanged; only how long «בודק…» stands · **Design:** [04c](04c-design-analytic.md) — the scheduler paragraph under "One configuration pool, completed after the render"

**Context.** The browser pre-play measured «בודק…» standing for **4.1–4.8 s** on three lines of the 572 exam (5, 8, 11), not ~0.5 s on one. Each seed was scheduled with `requestIdleCallback(…, { timeout: 200 })`, and 20 of 21 callbacks fired by the timeout. The vitest estimate came from the `setTimeout(0)` fallback, which a browser never takes. **Measured why** (Playwright, Chromium, headed and headless, this branch's dev server): the page renders nothing continuously — 0 animation frames per second and 0 running animations at rest, and an idle callback on the resting page fires in 8–14 ms. The starvation is the loop's OWN work: once a 7–74 ms seed has run and another is posted, Chromium grants no further idle period, so every later seed waits out the full timeout.

**Decision.** A slice is a plain macrotask — `scheduler.postTask({ priority: 'user-visible' })` where the browser has it, else a `MessageChannel` message (not clamped like nested timers), else `setTimeout(0)` — cancelled through its `AbortController` / port / timer when the figure changes. Still one seed per slice, so input and paint run between seeds. The plan's intent was always "yield between seeds", not "wait for idleness".

**The canvas label** «M(0, y_M)» seen beside «בודק…» is not a partial-pool reading: it is `figure.provenance` — the point's OWN givens, read syntactically inside `evaluate` («M on the y-axis» fixes x = 0 and says nothing about y) — identical before, during and after the check, and identical to before #1473. It is locked as pool-independent; whether the canvas should instead print a coordinate the WHOLE figure determines (y_M = 1 here, which the panel shows once settled) is a label-policy question for the operator, not part of this fix.

**Measured after** (Playwright, headless; headed within ±15 ms): 572 exam draw/settle — line 5: 11 ms / 34 ms; line 8: 25 ms / 60 ms; line 11: 148 ms / 424 ms; every other line settles with the draw (draws 13–272 ms). kite + circle + Z: no line shows «בודק…»; the worst line («נקודה Z», line 12) draws in 1728 ms — the render's own option walk, unchanged by #1473 in kind (it completes the pool inside the render). 0 idle callbacks and 0 timeouts on every line.

**Consequences.** `src-analytic/app/poolScheduler.ts` (`yieldScheduler` replaces `idleScheduler`). Locks: `issue-1473-knowledge-pool.test.ts` (the default scheduler completes the pool with `requestIdleCallback` stubbed to throw; a cancelled slice never runs), `issue-1473-mid-pool-render.test.tsx` (the canvas provenance is identical mid-check and settled on every 572 line).

## ADR-AG-185 — «בנקודות A ו-B»: both crossings in one sentence take the canonical order (#1512)

**Status:** accepted · 2026-09-30 · operator ruling 2026-09-29 on #1512, option **(a)** — *"arbitrary, and the user can change the letters if he wants"* · round #1571 · feature → PR

**Requirements:** [02c](02c-requirements-analytic.md) R85 — amended: one sentence may name both crossings; first letter = first root, second = second; never cycled; a pair that does not meet twice is refused on the sentence · **Design:** [04c](04c-design-analytic.md) — "Both crossings in one sentence are the two ordinal sentences" (after the ADR-AG-157 paragraph)

**Context.** Split from #1429's arm 4. «הישר l1 חותך את המעגל I בנקודות A ו-B» and «A ו-B נקודות החיתוך של הישר l1 עם המעגל I» were both `not-handled` (re-measured at `842ede39`), while the two ordinal sentences «A נקודת החיתוך הראשונה …» + «B נקודת החיתוך השנייה …» built. The open question was the letter assignment; the ruling fixed it to [ADR-AG-157](#adr-ag-157)'s canonical root order.

**Decision.**
1. **Lowering, no new rule semantics.** `bothCrossings` (called first in `intersectionSpellings`) reads the transitive verb («X חותך/חותכת/… את Y בנקודות A ו-B»), the plural verb («X ו-Y נחתכים בנקודות A ו-B»), the plural noun («[הנקודות] A ו-B [הן] נקודות החיתוך של X עם/ו-Y») and the English «X cuts/intersects/meets Y at [points] A and B», «X and Y intersect at A and B», «A and B are the intersection points of X and Y». Each lowers to the two ordinal sentences and re-parses them through `parseIntersection` — two declares, four incidences, two `crossing-nth` — all with the student's sentence as `src`. «בנקודות A ו-A» is `repeated-vertex`. A sub-sentence's owned refusal is returned with the whole sentence as detail; a `not-handled` one hands the line back to the chain.
2. **The one thing the pair of ordinals does not say: TWO points.** Measured: on a tangent line (`y=7` on a radius-3 circle at (3,4)) the two ordinals both hold at the touch (`nthHolds` answers true at a tangency, by ADR-AG-157's design), and the figure drew A and B 1e-3 apart with `faults: []`; with a FREE radius, seed 1 drove r onto the line and drew A = B = (0, 2), green. So the two selectors carry `both: true` and `nthHolds` first asks `meetsTwice`: a straight and a conic (two straights meet once; two conics have no order this module defines, so "A the first root" names nothing), not touching, and roots apart by more than `SOLVE_RESOLUTION · max(conic size, anchors' spread)` — the `openBoundFloor` rule of ADR-AG-167 am. 1, because a descent that approaches a double root stops within √SOLVE_TOL of it. Unjudgeable here (an anchor unplaced, a curve vacant) is `true`, as for the ordinal itself. Validity carries it: a free figure walks past the tangent seed; a figure with no freedom gets `unsatisfiable` on this sentence («לא נמצאה תצורה שבה מתקיים: "…"»).
3. **Rejected: a `distinct` selector on {A, B}.** Measured: it never fails when A and B are the figure's only points — its threshold is `1e-2 ×` the points' own spread, i.e. of their own distance. (That scale is a latent weakness of `distinct` in a figure with few points; it is not changed here — the kite and triangle callers carry more points — and is noted for a follow-up.)

**Not built.**
- **The contextual operand** «הישר l1 חותך את המעגל בנקודות A ו-B» (no name, one circle): refused `bad-operand`, as the single ordinal over a contextual operand already is (ADR-AG-157 — the pair is resolved at the fold, after the parser has built the selector).
